audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows contradicted their own why. whys[1] says her empowered Q 'still out-trades you' under a Skill row; whys[2], whys[3], whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] all say the stage is even or a skill lane, under rows that read Yone, Yone, Camille, Yone and Yone. The packet chart is Camille, Camille, then Skill for every remaining stage — which is exactly what the whys describe.
audit.why: A reader gets one answer from the chart and the opposite from the sentence beneath it.
audit.corrected: win[1]/phases[1].side = Camille; win[2] through win[6] and phases[2..6].side = Skill. Level 1 already read Camille.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names Hookshot as the thing to track on every screen and never states its cooldown, and never states the ultimate's.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s and The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s — the 16s window at rank 1 is the whole of your early commit timing.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interactions missing, both decisive. (a) Hookshot pulls Camille TO A WALL and leaps off it — in the open middle of the lane she has no gap-closer or knock-up at all. The page tells you to 'dodge her E' and lists 'Fight near walls' as a mistake, but never explains that terrain is the requirement. (b) Adaptive Defenses shields her against the damage TYPE that hit her, and Way of the Hunter adds magic damage on every second attack, so your mixed damage means her shield only ever covers half of what you are doing.
audit.why: Where you stand decides whether her engage exists, and the damage-type interaction is why burst reads on her are wrong.
audit.corrected: Wall requirement written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and mid; the shield interaction into spikes[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Tactical Sweep's outer cone heals her and nothing on the content layer mentions Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: The page's plan is short repeated trades, which is exactly what that heal refunds.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Camille must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online for both. Hold the wave near your side and take short trades only where Hookshot has no wall to grab.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Hookshot's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King evens it rather than winning it — force fights only while Hookshot is down.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Camille carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on and it is still a spacing lane. Camille carry threat 9/10 — close the game before the map decides for you.

edits.before: From level 3 on this settles into a genuine skill matchup. Camille's E (Hookshot) engage and true-damage second Q make her dangerous, but your Q dashes and E let you dodge her key hits and trade back. The swing point is her E cooldown — bait or dodge the Hookshot and you can commit; walk into it and you eat her full combo. Play the spacing tight and it stays even.
edits.after: From level 3 on this settles into a genuine skill matchup. Camille's Hookshot and true-damage second Q make her dangerous, but Hookshot has to anchor to a wall — hold the middle of the lane and her engage is simply not there. The swing point is its 16s cooldown: bait or dodge it and you can commit; walk into it and you eat her full combo.

edits.before: After first item this stays a skill lane. Camille builds bruiser and stays sticky, so don't over-commit into her E gap-close; trade in short bursts and reposition with your E before she lands her Q second hit.
edits.after: After first item this stays a skill lane. Adaptive Defenses only shields against the damage type that just hit her, and your passive adds magic on every second attack — keep both types flowing and half that shield is wasted.

edits.before: - Camille Hookshot: matchup-defining — Her engage/stun. Dodge with E. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Hookshot: 16s at rank 1, and it needs a wall — in open lane she has no engage. - Tactical Sweep: 15s, and the outer cone heals her, so bring Grievous Wounds. - The Hextech Ultimatum: 140s at rank 1.

edits.before: Her engage/stun. Dodge with E. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It anchors to a wall — stand in open lane and it cannot reach you.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Hookshot needs one; without a wall she has no gap-close at all.

edits.before: Isolate you with R Hextech Ultimatum for a kill
edits.after: Isolate you with The Hextech Ultimatum for a kill

notes: The packet's suspect name was real: the ability is 'The Hextech Ultimatum' with the article, and wants.foe[2] dropped it — fixed. The mechanical content of this entry was otherwise unusually sound; the failures were the level chart disagreeing with its own reasons in six of seven rows, and the wall requirement on Hookshot never being stated even though the page lists 'Fight near walls' as a common mistake.
